basic.title: How Languages Are Learned
basic.overview: Learn what helps people pick up a new language.

lesson.title: Input, practice, feedback
paragraphs: People learn a language by hearing and reading it in ways they can mostly understand, by using it themselves, and by getting feedback.
A good teacher designs lessons that include all three: something to listen to or read, a chance to speak or write, and kind, useful correction.
You will also see that learners differ. Some like to speak first, while others need time to listen.

basic.realWorld: Teachers constantly adjust how they explain things depending on who is in front of them.

task.prompt: Think of something in English that you learned and that really stuck. What helped you remember it?
task.note: There is no right answer. Reflecting on how you learn is the starting point for teaching others.

medium.title: Lesson Planning
medium.overview: Learn how to design a short lesson with a clear goal.

lesson.title: Goal, activity, check
paragraphs: A good lesson starts with a goal that says what students will be able to do at the end. Then you choose activities that lead to that goal, and a quick way to check whether it worked.

For a ten-minute lesson on ordering food, the goal could be that students can order a meal using three sentence patterns. The activity might be a role play, and the check is listening to pairs practise.
Planning is a skill you repeat many times until it becomes quick.

medium.realWorld: New teachers often write a short plan for every class they teach and adjust it afterwards.

task.prompt: Which lesson goal is the clearest?
options: Students can order a meal using three sentence patterns
task.note: Many people choose the second because you can see whether it was achieved. Clear goals make planning much easier.

deep.title: Teaching Practice
deep.overview: Try the real work of standing in front of a class.

lesson.title: Teaching in a real classroom
paragraphs: In teaching practice you assist an experienced teacher. You help groups, give feedback, and slowly take over small parts of the lesson.
Classroom moments are rarely perfect: a student stays silent, an activity ends early, or the room gets noisy. Teachers learn to stay calm and adjust.
After each lesson, you talk with your supervising teacher about what worked and what to try next.

deep.realWorld: Many schools welcome student teachers for several weeks, which shows what daily school life really feels like.

task.prompt: You ask a question and one student stays silent. Write what you would do next.
task.note: There is no right answer. Responding kindly in the moment is a core teaching skill.
